newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end sharply up on talk of firmer prices.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end sharply up on talk of firmer prices.

text.p: CME hog futures closed sharply higher on demand prompted by ideas of stronger cash hog and some pork prices. Locals dominated trade in pork bellies late and they closed with pared losses on short covering, traders said.

Hogs closed 1.400 to 0.050 cent a lb higher with June up most at 84.950 cents, a one week high. Pork bellies closed 0.375 cent lower to 1.000 higher with only fresh November up and July off most at 91.650 cents.
Talk that cash loins are showing increased demand and expectations of firmer cash hog prices early next week prompted buying, traders said.
"Loin trade had been slow and now they are moving," one trader said.
Although USDA details of loin sales were sketchy Thursday, traders said loin prices have risen $5 per cwt in the past week.

Hog runs were also not as large as expected Thursday despite delayed crop plantings and added time for farmers to ship hogs to market. This sparked ideas of steady-firm cash hog prices Friday and possibly higher markets early next week, traders said.
Anticipation of possible export business to the European Community following partial settlement over meat import regulations to the EU also lent support to hog futures.
"You could see a boost in the export numbers on the pork into the European Communities," said Jason Roose, analyst with U.S. Commodities Inc.

Rand Financials, Rosenthal Collins, Refco and Dean Witter bought June, traders said, and Rand also bought August and Cargill Investor Services sold October. Buy stops were hit near 84.000 cents, basis June, and there was scattered spreading of long hog futuers/short pork belly futures, pit sources said.

In hog options, locals bought June 81 straddle and sold the June 85 straddle and also spread long June 86 calls/short August 86 calls. Refco sold July and August 86 calls while Saul Stone sold June 89 calls, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures followed futures up early but turned lower on local pressure when cash bellies were posted lower at midday by the USDA. However, locals covered shorts late to pare losses, traders said.
Commercials sold early as high prices cut off demand for product with buyers citing reports of light product storings.
"We are not storing bellies - we may not store any more the rest of the year," one trader said.
The mixed ideas on cash fundamentals made for another day of choppy action, traders added.
LFG, Rand Financials and locals bought July early while Cargill sold. LFG sold late while Lind-Waldock bought, pit sources said.
